title: Chip Scaling Moves Beyond The Transistor
gist: SEMICON West 2026 showed the semiconductor industry passing $1 trillion years early, with SEMI now forecasting over $2 trillion by 2030 and 300mm fab equipment spend of $149B this year rising to $227B by 2029. Scaling is shifting from transistors to system-level co-optimization of packaging, photonics, power, test and AI, and the open question is how much manufacturing authority agentic AI is given.

insights.claim: SEMI's CEO forecast a semiconductor market above $2 trillion by 2030 and potentially $3 trillion by 2035, after the industry passed the $1 trillion-by-2030 path set in 2023 years early.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: The demand curve is far steeper than 2023 forecasts, supporting multi-year equipment and packaging capacity buildouts.
insights.locator: When SEMICON West gathered in San Francisco in 2023

insights.claim: SEMI projects 300mm fab equipment spending of $149 billion this year rising to $227 billion by 2029, with construction starting on 20 new 300mm fabs or production lines in 2026 alone.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Quantifies the WFE and fab construction runway for equipment vendors.
insights.locator: SEMI’s own projections show how steep that curve has become.

insights.claim: AI infrastructure drives much of the growth, but electrification, autonomous vehicles, robotics and industrial automation are adding semiconductor content, and the unusual part of this expansion is system complexity rather than just chip demand.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Growth drivers are broadening beyond data-center AI, though complexity is the binding constraint.
insights.locator: AI infrastructure is driving much of that growth

insights.claim: SEMICON West 2026 had a sold-out exhibit floor and more than 30,000 attendees.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Event attendance is a sentiment gauge for the upcycle.
insights.locator: SEMICON West 2026 returned to San Francisco

insights.claim: Improving any one of memory, packaging, optical interconnect or cooling can move the bottleneck elsewhere: more compute pressures memory bandwidth and power delivery, moving memory closer concentrates heat, and disaggregating a die adds interfaces to connect, power, cool and test.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Value accrues to firms that solve cross-domain bottlenecks, not single-component improvements.
insights.locator: The shift was apparent in conversations

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's Lalitha Immaneni argues packaging is no longer where semiconductor innovation ends but where system innovation begins, and described a move from design-technology co-optimization to system-technology co-optimization across silicon, packaging and platform.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Foundry differentiation is moving into packaging and platform integration, favoring integrated players like Intel Foundry.
insights.quote: Packaging is no longer simply the place where semiconductor innovation ends,
insights.locator: Packaging is no longer simply

insights.claim: Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi says engineering must be re-engineered to co-design across physics, materials, process, architecture, design, software and the AI model itself, because the model defines the workload.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: EDA demand extends from chip design into full-stack co-optimization including workload-aware design.
insights.locator: “We’ve started talking about how to re-engineer engineering

insights.claim: Imec CEO Patrick Vandenameele said adding accelerators and racks to AI data centers is not scaling in the traditional semiconductor sense and looks more like multiplication.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Challenges the framing of AI buildout as semiconductor scaling; efficiency gains still need technology progress.
insights.quote: It looks a little bit more like multiplication.
insights.locator: Patrick Vandenameele, CEO of imec

insights.claim: Marvell's Nitin Deshpande warns that packaging concepts only become business if they reach high volume with high yield, reliability and a supply chain that delivers parts in time.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Manufacturability, not concept, gates packaging revenue; watch yield and supply chain readiness.
insights.locator: “We can have very cool concepts

themes.theme: Agentic AI as operator in design and fab

insights.claim: Synopsys describes a progression from assistant copilots to generative capability to long-horizon autonomous agents where users specify an outcome rather than a prompt, and says it already has engagements where agents take a customer spec through verified RTL, work that took multiple engineers and months.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Evidence that agentic design flows are in customer engagements, a potential productivity step-change for EDA.
insights.locator: “We started from an assistant copilot

insights.claim: Lam Research's chief AI officer David Fried says the optimization space has become intractable, with a current Lam etcher having a potential recipe space on the order of 10^23 possibilities, which AI is needed to search.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Process complexity creates structural demand for AI tooling in fab process control.
insights.quote: The space that we’re optimizing in has exploded
insights.locator: David Fried, chief AI officer

insights.claim: Flagging an unusual process signature differs from letting AI alter a recipe, and predicting equipment degradation differs from stopping production; open questions include what decisions agents can make without approval and what evidence is required before autonomous decisions affect production.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Governance and validation of autonomous fab decisions will determine adoption pace; monitor vendor disclosures on agent authority.
insights.locator: Acting on what AI finds is where

insights.claim: The article argues the new question is no longer whether AI will design and manufacture semiconductors, since that is already happening, but how much authority engineers are prepared to give it.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Shifts the debate from adoption to trust boundaries.
insights.quote: The new question is how much authority engineers are prepared to give it.
insights.locator: The question coming out of SEMICON West

themes.theme: Known-good and test in advanced packaging

insights.claim: Known-good logic is moving outward from die to bridges, substrates and packages: Intel Foundry sorts even passive bridges, and ASE aims to confirm every layer is good before attaching the most expensive part.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Test and inspection content per package rises as assembly value rises, benefiting test and metrology vendors.
insights.locator: “Even though the bridge is a passive component

insights.claim: Some silicon and HBM combinations represent as much as $30,000 in value, and ASE uses AOI and X-ray extensively, with AI helping distinguish subtle differences across assemblies with as many as half a million joints.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: High value per assembly makes scrap intolerable and justifies heavy inspection spend.
insights.quote: Some silicon and HBM combinations can represent as much as $30,000 in value
insights.locator: Some silicon and HBM combinations

insights.claim: Bonding creates interfaces that did not exist when components were inspected, so some defects cannot be detected until a later step, shifting the sampling question from how much inspection maintains yield to how much uncertainty can be carried into the next step.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Inspection economics change toward uncertainty management across process steps.
insights.locator: Assembly complicates that goal.

insights.claim: Amkor says customers want optical tests on the top side and electrical tests on the bottom side of co-packaged optics packages with efficiency expectations, and that changing package size, weight and density affects test-cell time and insertions.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: CPO raises test complexity and cost; OSAT and test-equipment suppliers with optical capability stand to benefit.
insights.locator: “What our customers are demanding from OSATs

insights.claim: Microtronic retains wafer images as a historical record so defects found later can be traced to earlier process steps, with CEO Reiner Fenske saying history matters more than throughput.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Data retention and traceability are becoming product features in inspection.
insights.quote: throughput is a secondary issue, but having the history, that’s key
insights.locator: “The information that we gather is so valuable

insights.claim: Test is becoming less a final pass/fail gate than a continuous evidence trail, and AI can find patterns across that history only if data is tied to the right device, process step and physical context, which is harder as dies move through reconstituted wafers, panels and multi-die assemblies.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Data lineage across process steps is a prerequisite for AI yield gains.
insights.locator: Test is becoming less a final pass/fail gate

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's Huan Ma says co-packaged optics will scale only when optics are industrialized through advanced packaging, requiring six-degree-of-freedom precision bonding at semiconductor throughput and metrology of geometry, angles and positions that predict insertion loss and coupling efficiency.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: CPO timing hinges on assembly and metrology industrialization, not optics performance.
insights.quote: Co-packaged optics will not scale just because the optics work.
insights.locator: “For metrology and inspection, how do we measure

insights.claim: EV Group, Lam Research and Advantest each pointed to manufacturing burdens for photonics: alignment metrology across hundreds of dies in die-to-wafer integration, waveguide and modulator material and fiber coupling work, and high-volume electro-optical test as a remaining bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Identifies equipment segments with new photonics-driven demand.
insights.locator: The same issues surfaced across the show floor.

insights.claim: Intel's Ravi Mahajan says photonics assembly steps are not recoverable or reworkable, making yield limiters in assembly critical, but sees no intrinsic showstoppers since fiber attachment, once considered very difficult, has improved through process learning.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Insider view that CPO barriers are engineering practice, not physics, supporting a ramp thesis.
insights.quote: I cannot think of any intrinsic showstoppers in any of these processes,
insights.locator: “Coming through the door, you have an understanding

insights.claim: SEMICON West 2026 was the show's last scheduled run in San Francisco; SEMI signed a three-year agreement with Phoenix, with the next event at the Phoenix Convention Center on March 30 to April 1, 2027, starting a spring schedule.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Calendar marker for the next industry read, about five months away.
insights.locator: Conclusion: Five months to Phoenix

insights.claim: The author expects markers by the next show: agentic AI judged by which decisions agents are allowed to make, CPO moving from demonstrations to repeatable manufacturing, and high-NA EUV moving toward production while power delivery moves deeper into packages.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Checklist of milestones to monitor into spring 2027.
insights.locator: Agentic AI will be judged by which engineering
